title: Daily: 2026-11-13
story:
These logs are real. They come from hive, a honeypot on the internet, between 14:29 and 14:38 UTC on 2026-11-13.
Every line is a bot trying to break in. (IP addresses are replaced with example addresses, but everything else is what really happened.)

Your files in ~/challenge:
- `auth.log`: SSH login attempts, exactly as a real server logs them
- `honeypot-capture.txt`: the passwords the bots tried (only a honeypot can see these)
- `countries.txt`: which country each IP is in
hints: `grep`, `sort`, `uniq -c` and `sort -rn` answer most questions. Try `grep 'Failed password' ~/challenge/auth.log | head`.
Count per IP: `grep -o 'from [0-9.]*' ~/challenge/auth.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. Swap the pattern for usernames: `grep -o 'for [a-z ]*from'`.
`awk '{print $3}' ~/challenge/honeypot-capture.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` counts usernames, `$4` counts passwords. For countries, look each IP up in countries.txt with `grep`.
learned:
`198.51.100.14` alone made 89 of the 100 attempts, a typical brute-force bot working through a password list. `root` was the favorite username. Bots go for accounts that exist on almost every server.

In the last 24 hours hive caught 4,283 attempts from 187 networks.
Come back tomorrow for new logs, or see them live at https://xivlabs.tech/#attacks.

questions.prompt: Which IP address had the most failed SSH logins in auth.log?
Which username did the bots try most often?
How many different IP addresses tried to log in over SSH?
Use countries.txt: which country (two-letter code) sent the most SSH attempts?
